promises.quote: We will develop a process and protocol for escalation to be used within the borough of Stockport by the end of February 2019.
promises.summary: Develop escalation process for mental health referrals

promises.quote: Following review with the Lead Consultant [name redacted] the agreed target timescales for routine appointments is 12 weeks. Clear communication of the target timescales will form part of the action above.
promises.summary: Set 12-week target for routine psychiatric appointments

promises.quote: Stockport borough will produce an escalation protocol for staff to use when there is disagreement regarding the need for a face to face appointment with a psychiatrist. This will be completed by the end of February 2019.
promises.summary: Create escalation protocol for RAID referral disagreements

promises.quote: Pennine Care's alcohol liaison practitioners are moving to be based at Stepping Hill Hospital with the all age liaison mental health service and will form part of the same team which will significantly reduce the likelihood of any such concern arising again. promises.summary: Integrate alcohol liaison practitioners into mental health team

concerns.quote: He had long-term anxiety. Mental Health workers assessing him had repeatedly felt he needed to be seen by a psychiatrist. The referrals were rejected by the psychiatrist. There was no challenge or escalation process within the trust to deal with the situation.
concerns.hazard: lack of challenge or escalation process for mental health referrals

concerns.quote: A routine psychiatric out patient was offered after his mother indicated she would make a formal complaint. The inquest heard that there were no agreed target timescales for the offering of routine appointments.
concerns.hazard: absence of agreed target timescales for routine psychiatric appointments

concerns.quote: There had been a series of attendances at the emergency department and RAID referrals. The inquest heard that there was no documentation or rationale provided for why RAID did not refer him to a psychiatrist.
concerns.hazard: lack of documentation and rationale for RAID referral decisions

concerns.quote: On one admission to the acute hospital following an overdose, he was seen by an alcohol worker from the Mental Health Trust. There was no evidence that that worker had checked to see or understand any previous engagements with Mental Health Services. Information about that admission and encounter was not shared with wider mental health services even though they were part of the same trust.
concerns.hazard: failure to share information and coordinate care across mental health services
